title: Lumen Dock Playpen — first-touch compact personalization proto
content:
Quick brain dump — aim to capture a tiny, testable onboarding/personalization lane that can ship as a small opt-in experiment in 6 weeks. Not a full personalization system; a compact first-touch surface that adapts the initial assistant persona and response brevity based on 2 signals: (1) lightweight profile (explicit: first-visit quick form) and (2) implicit usage signal (first 3 interactions).

Problem:
- New users often tune out because default assistant is too verbose or shows irrelevant examples. Teams asking for a low-effort personalization entrypoint that avoids heavy data plumbing.

Goals (north star):
- Increase completion of first task (call-to-action click) by +8% for users in experiment cohort.
- Reduce average tokens consumed in first 3 interactions by 20% for users who prefer concise answers.
- Keep implementation surface minimal (no heavy server-side user-profile infra).

Proposed feature (Lumen Dock):
- Small modal on first open with 2 toggles: "I like short answers (bullet points)" and "Show examples I can copy" + optional role selector (e.g., researcher, manager, student). Persist via local storage and a small user attribute in existing auth profile (opt-in).
- Runtime: prompt templates pick a compact or expansive response framing; hosted API call adds a single metadata header (x-lumen-slate: compact|expanded|examples) used by routing and model variant selection.
- Quick server fallback: if header present and dedicated model unavailable, route to a cheaper quantized variant but keep instruction.

User stories:
- As a new user, I want to tell the assistant I prefer short answers so I can skim and act quickly.
- As a PM running the experiment, I want a toggle to enable cohort and view conversion/usage metrics.
- As an engineer, I want a low-friction opt-in that stores a flag and changes prompt_RENDER only, no profile heavy writes.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UI modal appears on first authenticated session; option persists across devices if user links account (otherwise local).
- API requests include lumen header when set.
- Console shows cohort metric: task-complete rate and token delta for cohort vs control.
- Experiment can be toggled on/off by a feature flag.

Instrumentation/metrics:
- metric: first_task_completion_rate (goal +8%)
- metric: avg_tokens_first_3_interactions (goal -20% for compact preference)
- metric: retention-7d delta for cohort (exploratory)

Rollout plan:
- Week 0–1: UI mocks + proto modal (frontend-only with client-side prompt injection).
- Week 2–3: Backend header plumbing + route tests (mock routing to quantized variant).
- Week 4: Small internal dogfood (10% staff).
- Week 5–6: 5% public cohort, monitor; iterate prompts and sample outputs.

Risks & open questions:
- Persisting preference across devices requires writing to profile table — privacy review? Maybe keep optional.
- Risk of content quality regressions when switching model variants; need a small eval set.
- Edge: users who flip preference mid-session — how to rehydrate KV cache safely?

Next actions (short):
- Create ticket JIRA-PLAT-2143 for backend header support (owner: Ishaan).
- Frontend prototype PR: create gh PR branch lumen-dock-ui (owner: Victor).
- Small eval: author 12 seed prompts that should remain stable under compact framing — add to micro-eval harness.
- Sync with privacy/security (quick ping to @sec with doc link).

Notes to self:
- Keep copy in modal extremely short; avoid granular settings in MVP.
- Consider a follow-up to auto-detect brevity preference from interaction speed (longer reads = prefer examples?).
- If initial experiment lifts conversion, consider adding automatic signal extraction to reduce friction.

Scribbles (random):
- Prompt template examples: "You are concise assistant. Answer in 2–3 bullets and include a one-line TL;DR." vs "You are an assistant that provides examples and copyable snippet blocks."

Links referenced: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ONRAMP/Lumen-dock, JIRA-PLAT-2143, github PR #7

TODOs (inline):

- [ ] Add micro-eval seeds to eval repo
- [ ] Draft short privacy blurb for modal

End of pad — capturing fuzzy thoughts so I can hand off a tidy PRD later.
